title: A finite module killed elementwise by a multiplicative set is killed by one element of it
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $S\subseteq A$ a multiplicative subset and $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] such that $S^{-1}M=0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], i.e. for every $m\in M$ there is $t\in S$ with $tm=0$. Then there is $s\in S$ with $sM=0$ (that is, $sm=0$ for all $m\in M$).

source.place: Exercises, Exercise 076A (exercise-localize-finite-module-zero, line 745: finite M with S^{-1}M=0 has f in S with M_f=0; the form sM=0 is the one used in the proof of Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma 07FC, smoothing.tex line 2301: 'Hence we can find an s in S such that s annihilates Q').
